project.name: waydroid-container
project.description: Waydroid (official LineageOS-based vendor Android image) run headless inside a Docker container, decoupled from the live desktop Wayland session — the ghost-process bug that got the original desktop-session Waydroid decommissioned CANNOT recur, because the container's lifecycle is independent of the desktop session. Renders into a nested headless sway (wlroots) compositor exported over VNC via wayvnc — Debian bookworm's weston 10.0.1 rdp-backend.so was tried first but has a confirmed dead-connection bug (accepts the TCP handshake, never services the RDP protocol negotiation — isolated via fresh-container + single-client + thread-count + backtrace tests, 2026-07-04) and has no vnc-backend.so either; sway+wayvnc is the standard, actively-maintained combo for headless-Wayland VNC. The host connects with a VNC viewer in a window to see it (same GUI-bound up=boot+attach/down=teardown-on-close pattern as da_redroid, just a different display transport — scrcpy mirrors ADB/SurfaceFlinger, VNC mirrors a Wayland compositor). Exists because Waydroid's vendor image is memfd-based (no real /dev/ashmem needed) since 1.2.1+, so Chromium-based apps that crash under redroid (this host's mainline kernel has no ashmem) should work here — that's the whole point of this project.

container._doc: Docker container knobs. image is OUR built image (Debian + waydroid + sway + wayvnc), never a public upstream tag — Waydroid has no official Docker image. base_image is what we build FROM.
container._doc_vnc: wayvnc 0.5.0 (Debian bookworm) binds this port with NO authentication by default (matches the prior RDP backend's no-app-login model) — port is bound to 127.0.0.1 only regardless (never exposed beyond the host). sway runs headless (WLR_BACKENDS=headless, no real GPU/input device) via seatd for the minimal libseat requirement wlroots still initializes even headless.
container._doc_memory_reservation: docker --memory-reservation (a SOFT limit, not a hard cap) — under host-wide memory pressure the kernel prefers reclaiming from cgroups that exceed their own reservation first, so this container's Android processes (system_server/zygote) get priority over other, unreserved cgroups instead of being starved by them. Confirmed necessary: on this host, concurrent unrelated processes pushed available memory under 1GB, and Android's own lmkd was crash-looping system_server every ~5s (dmesg: repeated 'Successfully killed process cgroup uid 1000') — a genuine host memory-contention bug, not a waydroid-container defect.
container._doc_stop_timeout: docker stop's grace period before SIGKILL. The entrypoint's SIGTERM trap does an ORDERED teardown (waydroid session stop -> waydroid container stop -> wayvnc -> sway -> seatd -> pulseaudio -> both dbus daemons) so every stack this container started actually exits cleanly rather than being cut off mid-shutdown by docker's 10s default — a SIGKILL mid-`waydroid container stop` can corrupt Android's persistent /data (the ghost-process class of bug that got the original desktop-session Waydroid decommissioned).

waydroid._doc: waydroid CLI invocation knobs (manual, non-systemd — 'waydroid container start' + 'waydroid session start' are direct commands, no systemctl dependency, confirmed from docs.waydro.id/usage/waydroid-command-line-options). gpu_mode was removed 2026-07-08: waydroid 1.6.2's waydroid.cfg (vendor_type MAINLINE) has no gpu_mode key at all — the entrypoint's sed patch for it was a confirmed silent no-op (verified live: `cat waydroid.cfg` has no such field). GPU accel is whatever this vendor image defaults to; there is currently no user-facing toggle in this waydroid version.
